Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 18, "heading": "CHAPTER 16. I AM A NEW BOY IN MORE SENSES THAN ONE", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 16, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u018-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 16. I AM A NEW BOY IN MORE SENSES THAN ONE", "sha256": "3f536d5d6a328df91e8aca1c21ff744b8b97ba8b605a0ea0c5add643ef57f8a2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Next morning, after breakfast, I entered on school life again. I went, accompanied by Mr. Wickfield, to the scene of my future studies—a grave building in a courtyard, with a learned air about it that seemed very well suited to the stray rooks and jackdaws who came down from the Cathedral towers to walk with a clerkly bearing on the grass-plot—and was introduced to my new master, Doctor Strong.", "sha256": "8ba158f3d7e1bb4d313c4114162b41e74606f94734d8bc34f2f34ac65e6b1393", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Doctor Strong looked almost as rusty, to my thinking, as the tall iron rails and gates outside the house; and almost as stiff and heavy as the great stone urns that flanked them, and were set up, on the top of the red-brick wall, at regular distances all round the court, like sublimated skittles, for Time to play at. He was in his library (I mean Doctor Strong was), with his clothes not particularly well brushed, and his hair not particularly well combed; his knee-smalls unbraced; his long black gaiters unbuttoned; and his shoes yawning like two caverns on the hearth-rug. Turning upon me a lustreless eye, that reminded me of a long-forgotten blind old horse who once used to crop the grass, and tumble over the graves, in Blunderstone churchyard, he said he was glad to see me: and then he gave me his hand; which I didn’t know what to do with, as it did nothing for itself.", "sha256": "38576b95514b41eefa41713c82018a946d6184d525d012f45165b1f583dc3bb7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But, sitting at work, not far from Doctor Strong, was a very pretty young lady—whom he called Annie, and who was his daughter, I supposed—who got me out of my difficulty by kneeling down to put Doctor Strong’s shoes on, and button his gaiters, which she did with great cheerfulness and quickness. When she had finished, and we were going out to the schoolroom, I was much surprised to hear Mr. Wickfield, in bidding her good morning, address her as ‘Mrs. Strong’; and I was wondering could she be Doctor Strong’s son’s wife, or could she be Mrs. Doctor Strong, when Doctor Strong himself unconsciously enlightened me.", "sha256": "12a264ba66564e59e70bfc742c4e265e289bf4855d8501d44c78aff988bd054c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘By the by, Wickfield,’ he said, stopping in a passage with his hand on my shoulder; ‘you have not found any suitable provision for my wife’s cousin yet?’", "sha256": "920c18a4af6b67c435d190e1748d6466a0e7b0742d881ea8b41f15b6df6867b4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ said Mr. Wickfield. ‘No. Not yet.’", "sha256": "4fb5a0363e49c1bba421736fbe315abfb4f8d751ca7ac3f0709b4e91de721bd7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I could wish it done as soon as it can be done, Wickfield,’ said Doctor Strong, ‘for Jack Maldon is needy, and idle; and of those two bad things, worse things sometimes come. What does Doctor Watts say,’ he added, looking at me, and moving his head to the time of his quotation, ‘“Satan finds some mischief still, for idle hands to do.”’", "sha256": "a8af5770cd49e16aae8bd871958fddf2ffa0fea42efe648f2f15b3b561222775", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Egad, Doctor,’ returned Mr. Wickfield, ‘if Doctor Watts knew mankind, he might have written, with as much truth, “Satan finds some mischief still, for busy hands to do.” The busy people achieve their full share of mischief in the world, you may rely upon it. What have the people been about, who have been the busiest in getting money, and in getting power, this century or two? No mischief?’", "sha256": "159606587dd3bb2e73a4497b84a736f09a7fc61434b2066a6912d530fa2c9e28", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Jack Maldon will never be very busy in getting either, I expect,’ said Doctor Strong, rubbing his chin thoughtfully.", "sha256": "a25cc2c9bd811d8452dbc322665b393b7c64f3b1f193bb70e54eafd7361b27b2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Perhaps not,’ said Mr. Wickfield; ‘and you bring me back to the question, with an apology for digressing. No, I have not been able to dispose of Mr. Jack Maldon yet. I believe,’ he said this with some hesitation, ‘I penetrate your motive, and it makes the thing more difficult.’", "sha256": "b96d7bd4cf4aac89e63d736393606fe5db6961423c273192d160b04aab25a7b6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My motive,’ returned Doctor Strong, ‘is to make some suitable provision for a cousin, and an old playfellow, of Annie’s.’", "sha256": "57e891d484be3f4ac1ac669eb9e97034fb10663060a78f1c7092de4441f1b581", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Yes, I know,’ said Mr. Wickfield; ‘at home or abroad.’", "sha256": "44a0a3244ad366a52ff32dc241c28364c843ca863b9218691e53e6a59d09b1d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Aye!’ replied the Doctor, apparently wondering why he emphasized those words so much. ‘At home or abroad.’", "sha256": "e4544058e8b78c7da784921f6ddb1a857bf8f25696bc697856c6b7b2cfbb1daa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Your own expression, you know,’ said Mr. Wickfield. ‘Or abroad.’", "sha256": "4bcda12c3a39d5f93d8927441647ba33fb8246a7f78f8106606c8855f249bfa0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Surely,’ the Doctor answered. ‘Surely. One or other.’", "sha256": "8f9802cdf2b1e93a015e0f1854af40cb4a0148a902c3a3f6ce2b0e8820d00dce", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘One or other? Have you no choice?’ asked Mr. Wickfield.", "sha256": "21304754d46b87c68c00b8b773554a269261feb753d0ff21ed6d8c1545343aea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ returned the Doctor.", "sha256": "5089ee45de06e3a8cdf2fb53c2230d27c6bc80d147b2f61164b4462864eb16ee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No?’ with astonishment.", "sha256": "812df63e4a616559c98aaa95d95667315223c85430c25145ca10948b09c87c27", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Not the least.’", "sha256": "ec50cac83bc2da2c5027419c162d9e1637ffd039c339f5eff2137f2aa989b2f9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No motive,’ said Mr. Wickfield, ‘for meaning abroad, and not at home?’", "sha256": "6a7ff81d5c3354594c8a159e51e4e1f9e3a315b2df5d8e88580511b12fe1b762", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ returned the Doctor.", "sha256": "5089ee45de06e3a8cdf2fb53c2230d27c6bc80d147b2f61164b4462864eb16ee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am bound to believe you, and of course I do believe you,’ said Mr. Wickfield. ‘It might have simplified my office very much, if I had known it before. But I confess I entertained another impression.’", "sha256": "753dbe7f702d679dee0e4f4737c052b041ef90fe0aa1a1a35922389cd2a0c945", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Doctor Strong regarded him with a puzzled and doubting look, which almost immediately subsided into a smile that gave me great encouragement; for it was full of amiability and sweetness, and there was a simplicity in it, and indeed in his whole manner, when the studious, pondering frost upon it was got through, very attractive and hopeful to a young scholar like me. Repeating ‘no’, and ‘not the least’, and other short assurances to the same purport, Doctor Strong jogged on before us, at a queer, uneven pace; and we followed: Mr. Wickfield, looking grave, I observed, and shaking his head to himself, without knowing that I saw him.", "sha256": "395d5f2c4410513e44840231fe32a0a17ddfd48eceb4b68f2db3dfc0e6fe6ab5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The schoolroom was a pretty large hall, on the quietest side of the house, confronted by the stately stare of some half-dozen of the great urns, and commanding a peep of an old secluded garden belonging to the Doctor, where the peaches were ripening on the sunny south wall. There were two great aloes, in tubs, on the turf outside the windows; the broad hard leaves of which plant (looking as if they were made of painted tin) have ever since, by association, been symbolical to me of silence and retirement. About five-and-twenty boys were studiously engaged at their books when we went in, but they rose to give the Doctor good morning, and remained standing when they saw Mr. Wickfield and me.", "sha256": "fc170f539e8a9a0deeb557d47fc56bc73d8c1a110a22bc8ad4f94d6d816c5e9d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘A new boy, young gentlemen,’ said the Doctor; ‘Trotwood Copperfield.’", "sha256": "b6963cea6bbb7f1e94ad37b61f176d3a602a070d765cfe0a70e564925b3aaeb2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "One Adams, who was the head-boy, then stepped out of his place and welcomed me. He looked like a young clergyman, in his white cravat, but he was very affable and good-humoured; and he showed me my place, and presented me to the masters, in a gentlemanly way that would have put me at my ease, if anything could.", "sha256": "6c01cb45d410ca3c8b92300c64ab632eeee671a4942b4421df9a4ebae1fc536e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It seemed to me so long, however, since I had been among such boys, or among any companions of my own age, except Mick Walker and Mealy Potatoes, that I felt as strange as ever I have done in my life. I was so conscious of having passed through scenes of which they could have no knowledge, and of having acquired experiences foreign to my age, appearance, and condition as one of them, that I half believed it was an imposture to come there as an ordinary little schoolboy. I had become, in the Murdstone and Grinby time, however short or long it may have been, so unused to the sports and games of boys, that I knew I was awkward and inexperienced in the commonest things belonging to them. Whatever I had learnt, had so slipped away from me in the sordid cares of my life from day to night, that now, when I was examined about what I knew, I knew nothing, and was put into the lowest form of the school. But, troubled as I was, by my want of boyish skill, and of book-learning too, I was made infinitely more uncomfortable by the consideration, that, in what I did know, I was much farther removed from my companions than in what I did not. My mind ran upon what they would think, if they knew of my familiar acquaintance with the King’s Bench Prison? Was there anything about me which would reveal my proceedings in connexion with the Micawber family—all those pawnings, and sellings, and suppers—in spite of myself? Suppose some of the boys had seen me coming through Canterbury, wayworn and ragged, and should find me out? What would they say, who made so light of money, if they could know how I had scraped my halfpence together, for the purchase of my daily saveloy and beer, or my slices of pudding? How would it affect them, who were so innocent of London life, and London streets, to discover how knowing I was (and was ashamed to be) in some of the meanest phases of both? All this ran in my head so much, on that first day at Doctor Strong’s, that I felt distrustful of my slightest look and gesture; shrunk within myself whensoever I was approached by one of my new schoolfellows; and hurried off the minute school was over, afraid of committing myself in my response to any friendly notice or advance.", "sha256": "4d044016ffb3356fd20df90d88b9d0126f6ba006029a69cf34ff5db5e4ff8535", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But there was such an influence in Mr. Wickfield’s old house, that when I knocked at it, with my new school-books under my arm, I began to feel my uneasiness softening away. As I went up to my airy old room, the grave shadow of the staircase seemed to fall upon my doubts and fears, and to make the past more indistinct. I sat there, sturdily conning my books, until dinner-time (we were out of school for good at three); and went down, hopeful of becoming a passable sort of boy yet.", "sha256": "40af5b04aae9095364be008391e4fe6ab32f6e90f3b36019895cea2c72a43462", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Agnes was in the drawing-room, waiting for her father, who was detained by someone in his office. She met me with her pleasant smile, and asked me how I liked the school. I told her I should like it very much, I hoped; but I was a little strange to it at first.", "sha256": "ebbe7e1c9092a7ec233958129338eb3460f10d018813b3fb281a5cce89aad46c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You have never been to school,’ I said, ‘have you?’ ‘Oh yes! Every day.’", "sha256": "3a88396026aeade30e673d48e9774feaba0842a454b0943fdda35b855726b149", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Ah, but you mean here, at your own home?’", "sha256": "943e226c070acfd2e22628162d1ad523342edac86932fbf5868dd228e6ccf4c4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u018-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Papa couldn’t spare me to go anywhere else,’ she answered, smiling and shaking her head. ‘His housekeeper must be in his house, you know.’", "sha256": "973469a959d0cbbbfaea74be080702ab4d5e44f8eb94815ab3b94394ea356e39", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[23]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
